[tense] - Someone is going to poison my plant if I don’t stop it!

- The sniper’s weapon is hidden in the warehouse!

- Even after I managed to dismantle all the her other plans, the Destroyer of Suns came herself to my flat at midnight, and murdered the sunflower. If only I found out her identity...

- I saw my neighbour talking to the girl I met on the Main Avenue, inside her school!

- The girl from the main avenue told me her mother is a teacher at the school, and her father is a security guard at the water processing plant.

... knocked on her door.

She didn’t answer. I guess she wasn’t at home? I should try again later.

She opened it.
''Hey, neighbour, it’s you'' she said, eyeing me suspiciously. ''Did you need anything in particular?''
The memories of her, dressed only with dynamite and abseiling down my flat, rushed into my mind. I won’t deny I got a tad nervous, and probably gave myself away by saying ''Eh...um... Hello! Where did you learn how to abseil?'' To which she answered 
''I’m a firefighter''
That was more that I could handle and rushed back home to the sweet solace of my sunflower.

She opened it.
''Hey, it’s you!'' She said.
''Err...um... Hello!'' I replied, not really knowing what to say ''Soo, what is that you do with your life?'' To which she answered 
''I’m a firefighter''
 That was more that I could handle and rushed back home to the solace of my sunflower.

a gardener, tending to his plants. I hold a deep respect for all gardeners, but, given the circumstances, I couldn’t help but mistrust him. After all, if you know how to keep a plant alive, you also know how best to kill it. I had to ask the question.
“What’s your favourite flower?” I heard right then, interrupting my thoughts. I raised my head and saw the gardener smiling at me. There was a serene sadness in his eyes.

“Sunflowers”

“Su... Roses”

“Hey, that’s what I wanted to ask!”

... a gardener, tending to his plants, or at least trying to. At the moment, he was mostly looking at his empty water hose with a mourning face. 
“They cut the water”, he said sadly, as if he had just woken from a beautiful dream. “How am I supposed to water my plants now?”.

“I heard there was a problem at the water processing plant”.

“Cheer up, it should only last a few hours”.

“I like flowers”.

Then they started talking about a new girl that had recently moved to town and was attending second grade.
Apparently, her mother was a new teacher at the school. They all seemed to like the new girl, but they complained that she always seemed to be busy for some reason, and they almost never got a chance to play with her.
After a while I got tired of their talk and went home.

“Sunflowers,” I replied without hesitation. The gardener’s smile broadened, and he said, “yes, you do look like the sunflower type. Not many left around these days, huh?” he added with a mournful voice. 
“No, sadly not,” I agreed, wondering if I had given myself away too soon. The gardener looked at me once more with that rueful smile, and said “here, take these gardenias. A gift, from a fellow lover of flowers to another”.
I thanked him and left, not knowing quite what to make of him.

“I heard there was a problem at the water processing plant”. 
As soon as I said those words, he looked up at me with a shine to his eyes. “Really? Well, we can’t allow that, can we? No, no, no. I will have to go there immediately. Oh, yes. They shall hear about this. What kind of water processing plant stops processing the water for my plants on such an important day? Oh, no, no, no, I will have none of that”.

I took both.

I took the sandwich

I took nothing.

“He kept on muttering to himself as he stood up and left in direction to the water plant, but all I heard were some isolated words like “fire”, “massacre” and “thermonuclear punishment”. 
After he left, I noticed he had forgotten some recently cut flowers and a sandwich.

Seemed like he wasn’t going to need them anyway, where he was going.

Approach him, but as soon as he noticed me he stopped talking abruptly and shot me a guilty glance. All I could overhear was ”my love”, “destroy” and “warehouse”, but that was enough. Why else would he be looking at me with such a look of guilt painted all over his face?

“You’re the sunflower murderer!”

“You, uhm... what were you talking about just now?”
